ticket.title: storypole update should append to a description instead of requiring the whole text back
ticket.description:
Observed 2026-11-06: recording progress on GB-204, OF-5 and GB-79 meant reading the full description with 'show --json', concatenating in python, and writing it back with --desc, four times. The description is the ticket's memory and it is now several kilobytes on GB-204, so every append re-sends the whole thing through the model's context - expensive, and one truncation away from destroying the history. A '--append-desc <TEXT>' (or '--desc-from -' reading stdin) would make the normal workflow one cheap call, and makes it impossible to lose the earlier text by accident.

Live check: this paragraph was appended by --append-desc rather than resending the whole field.
acceptance_criteria:
DONE 2026-11-07, commit 6285754 (storypole). `storypole update --append-desc <TEXT>` and `--append-desc-file <PATH|->` append a paragraph instead of requiring the whole description back. `--desc` conflicts with both, because replace and append in one call is ambiguous and the ambiguity would resolve silently.

Why it matters: recording progress on three tickets in this session meant reading the description with `show --json`, concatenating in python and writing it back with `--desc`, four times. Each round trip could lose the earlier text, and one nearly did.

Separator behaviour is the part with tests, four of them: exactly one blank line between paragraphs; no leading newline when the description was empty; no accumulation of trailing whitespace across repeated appends, since every append would otherwise add another separator to the end of the field; and an empty addition changes nothing.

Found while verifying, filed separately: `storypole show` prints no description at all, and `show --json` returns a briefing envelope rather than the task. That combination is why the append initially looked broken - I read a task snapshot from the ledger, and TaskUpdated carries a delta, so the snapshot could not contain the answer. The same error as GB-281: query something that cannot contain the result, then believe its silence. `list --json` shows the replayed state and the paragraph is there.

Tier 2: clippy -p storypole-cli --all-targets -D warnings clean, 7 tests green in the package, installed to PATH before the live check rather than after the chain was wired to depend on it.

task.title: storypole update should append to a description instead of requiring the whole text back
task.description: Observed 2026-11-06: recording progress on GB-204, OF-5 and GB-79 meant reading the full description with 'show --json', concatenating in python, and writing it back with --desc, four times. The description is the ticket's memory and it is now several kilobytes on GB-204, so every append re-sends the whole thing through the model's context - expensive, and one truncation away from destroying the history. A '--append-desc <TEXT>' (or '--desc-from -' reading stdin) would make the normal workflow one cheap call, and makes it impossible to lose the earlier text by accident.

acceptance_criteria: in one session: every 'storypole update --criterion' overwrites nothing but is hard to use for capture
and there is no append-only way to record a date-stamped note. Observations worth adding to this ticket: (1) update takes one criterion at a time

so recording three findings from one run means three invocations and three chances to mistype a key; (2) a criterion passed twice silently duplicates rather than erroring; (3) the cost was paid at least six times today
each time with a 1-2k character shell-quoted blob. An --append-desc plus a repeatable --criterion would have saved most of it
and a --criterion-from-file (or - for stdin) would remove the quoting risk entirely - I had two commits mangled by shell escaping today
one of which silently committed nothing.

same class as the escaping failures already recorded here: backticks inside a double-quoted --criterion argument are SHELL-EXECUTED by zsh before storypole sees them. Two terms in a GB-278 criterion were silently replaced by empty output; the command still exited 0
so the damage was invisible until I read the ticket back. That is a third silent-corruption path through this interface today
alongside mangled multi-flag commits and an aborted add. It strengthens the case for --criterion-from-file (or - for stdin): the shell never touches the content
so no escaping rule can be forgotten.
criterion read from a file: commas, backticks `like this`, and "quotes" survive intact
